source.text: לַמְנַצֵּ֬חַ עַֽל־שׁוֹשַׁנִּ֬ים לְדָוִֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: For the director, on Shoshannim. Of David.

en.L: For the director: on shoshannim. Of David.
en.B: For the music director. On shoshannim. Of David.
en.R: For the leader of the music. To the tune "Lilies". By David.

decisions.reason: The title is part of the Hebrew text and is counted as verse 1, so the verse numbers here are one higher than in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: the director: the one who leads the music
decisions.reason: As in 4:1, probably the leader of the temple music.

alternatives: to the tune of a song called Lilies
decisions.reason: As in 45:1, the word means lilies. It may name a tune, or an instrument; the musical sense is no longer known.

decisions.choice: a psalm the New Testament often quotes
decisions.reason: After Psalm 22, this is the psalm the New Testament quotes most often. Its innocent sufferer, hated without cause and given vinegar to drink, is read there of Jesus (John 2:17; 15:25; 19:28-29; Romans 15:3), and its curses of the enemies are applied to those who rejected him (Acts 1:20; Romans 11:9-10). In the psalm itself the speaker is a human sufferer who also confesses his own folly (verse 6).
Readable gives one likely sense of the term (m3).

source.text: הוֹשִׁיעֵ֥נִי אֱלֹהִ֑ים כִּ֤י בָ֖אוּ מַ֣יִם עַד־נָֽפֶשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: Save me, God, for waters have come up to [the] neck.

en.L: Save me, God, \q for [the] waters have come up to [my] neck.
en.B: Rescue me, God, \q for the water has risen to my throat.
en.R: Save me, God! \q The water is up to my neck.

decisions.reason: The word is nefesh, which can mean the throat or neck, the place of breathing; so also in Jonah 2. The water is about to close over him.
Deep water and mud are pictures of deadly danger (18:17; 40:3; 124:4-5). The picture runs through verses 2-3 and 15-16.

source.text: טָבַ֤עְתִּי׀בִּיוֵ֣ן מְ֭צוּלָה וְאֵ֣ין מָעֳמָ֑ד בָּ֥אתִי בְמַעֲמַקֵּי־מַ֝֗יִם וְשִׁבֹּ֥לֶת שְׁטָפָֽתְנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: I have sunk in [the] mire of [the] depth, and there is no standing; I have come into [the] depths of water, and a flood has swept over me.

en.L: I have sunk in [the] mire of the deep, and there is no foothold; \q I have come into [the] depths of water, and a flood has swept over me.
en.B: I am sinking in deep mud with nothing to stand on; \q I have gone down into deep water, and the current is carrying me away.
en.R: I am sinking in deep mud. There is nothing solid to stand on. \q I am in deep water, and the flood is washing over me.

decisions.reason: The word (yawen) is the mud at the bottom of a pit or swamp (40:3).
The word (shibbolet) is a stream in flood, strong enough to carry a person off.

source.text: יָגַ֣עְתִּי בְקָרְאִי֮ נִחַ֪ר גְּר֫וֹנִ֥י כָּל֥וּ עֵינַ֑י מְ֝יַחֵ֗ל לֵאלֹהָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: I am weary with my crying; my throat is parched; my eyes have failed, waiting for my God.

en.L: I am weary with my crying; my throat is parched; \q my eyes have failed, \q waiting for my God.
en.B: I am exhausted from calling out; my throat is burning dry. \q My eyes have grown dim \q from watching for my God.
en.R: I have cried for help until I am tired. My throat is dry and sore. \q I have watched for my God so long that my eyes are worn out.

decisions.choice: my eyes have failed: worn out with watching
decisions.reason: Eyes that "fail" are tired and dim from looking long for help that has not come (119:82; Lamentations 4:17).
The verb (charar) is to be scorched; his throat is raw from calling.

source.text: רַבּ֤וּ׀מִשַּׂעֲר֣וֹת רֹאשִׁי֮ שֹׂנְאַ֪י חִ֫נָּ֥ם עָצְמ֣וּ מַ֭צְמִיתַי אֹיְבַ֣י שֶׁ֑קֶר אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־גָ֝זַ֗לְתִּי אָ֣ז אָשִֽׁיב׃

records.literal_gloss: More than [the] hairs of my head are those who hate me without cause; mighty are those who destroy me, my enemies [of] falsehood; what I did not steal, then I must restore.

en.L: More than the hairs of my head are those who hate me without cause; \q mighty are those who would destroy me, my enemies [who speak] falsehood; \q what I did not steal, I must then restore.
en.B: There are more people hating me for no reason than hairs on my head; \q strong are the ones who seek my ruin, my enemies with their lies. \q Am I to repay what I never took?
en.R: More people hate me than there are hairs on my head, and they have no reason to. \q My enemies are strong and tell lies about me. They want to destroy me. \q They make me pay back things I never stole.

decisions.reason: Jesus says that the word written in their law is fulfilled in him: "They hated me without a cause." The same words are found in 35:19.

decisions.choice: my enemies of falsehood: enemies who lie
decisions.reason: The word (sheqer) means falsehood. They are enemies on false grounds, who accuse him with lies.

decisions.choice: what I did not steal, I must restore
alternatives: must I now restore what I did not steal?
decisions.reason: He is made to pay back what he never took, perhaps as a proverb for being punished though innocent. It may also be read as a bitter question.

source.text: אֱֽלֹהִ֗ים אַתָּ֣ה יָ֭דַעְתָּ לְאִוַּלְתִּ֑י וְ֝אַשְׁמוֹתַ֗י מִמְּךָ֥ לֹא־נִכְחָֽדוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: God, you know my folly, and my guilty deeds from you are not hidden.

en.L: God, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} know my folly, \q and my guilty deeds are not hidden from {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.
en.B: God, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} know my foolishness; \q none of my guilt is hidden from {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.
en.R: God, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} know the foolish things I have done. \q You can see all my sins.

decisions.choice: folly and guilt: he does not claim to be sinless
decisions.reason: The psalmist is hated without cause (verse 5), yet he admits his own foolishness and wrongs before God, who sees them all. He asks for help on the basis of God's love, not his own innocence (verse 14).

decisions.choice: guilty deeds: wrongs that bring guilt
decisions.reason: The word ('ashmah) is guilt, here in the plural for the wrongs that caused it.

source.text: אַל־יֵ֘בֹ֤שׁוּ בִ֨י׀קֹוֶיךָ֮ אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֗ה צְבָ֫א֥וֹת אַל־יִכָּ֣לְמוּ בִ֣י מְבַקְשֶׁ֑יךָ אֱ֝לֹהֵ֗י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Let not those who wait for you be ashamed in me, Lord YHWH of hosts; let not those who seek you be humiliated in me, God of Israel.

en.L: Let not those who wait for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} be ashamed because of me, my Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} of hosts; \q let not those who seek {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} be humiliated because of me, \q God of Israel.
en.B: May no one who waits for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} be shamed through me, Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} of Armies; \q may no one who seeks {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} be humiliated through me, \q God of Israel.
en.R: Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} of Armies, people who trust {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are waiting for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} help. Do not let them be embarrassed because of me. \q God of Israel, do not let those who look to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} be shamed because of me.

decisions.choice: ashamed because of me: let down by my fall
decisions.reason: If God abandons him, those who trust God will be ashamed, as if their hope were empty. His rescue matters for all the faithful.

decisions.choice: Lord GOD of hosts: 'Adonai YHWH tseba'ot
decisions.reason: Here the title "Lord" stands with the name and "of hosts". As where "the Lord" stands with the name elsewhere, the name is written GOD.

The title (YHWH tseba'ot) names the LORD as commander of the armies of heaven, his angels and the stars (1 Kings 22:19; Isaiah 40:26), and of Israel's army (1 Samuel 17:45). Literal keeps the older "hosts"; Balanced and Readable say "Armies", as in Isaiah.
Readable says what they wait for.

source.text: כִּֽי־עָ֭לֶיךָ נָשָׂ֣אתִי חֶרְפָּ֑ה כִּסְּתָ֖ה כְלִמָּ֣ה פָנָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: For on account of you I have borne reproach; humiliation has covered my face.

en.L: For on account of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} I have borne reproach; \q humiliation has covered my face.
en.B: Because of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} I have carried scorn; \q humiliation covers my face.
en.R: I am insulted because I belong to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. \q My face burns with shame.

decisions.choice: for your sake: suffering for God
decisions.reason: His suffering is not only for his own wrongs: he is mocked because of his loyalty to God (verse 10; Jeremiah 15:15).
Shame is pictured as a covering over the face (44:16).
Readable says how his suffering is "for God's sake" (m1).

source.text: מ֭וּזָרהָיִ֣יתִי לְאֶחָ֑י וְ֝נָכְרִ֗י לִבְנֵ֥י אִמִּֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Estranged I have become to my brothers and a foreigner to [the] sons of my mother.

en.L: Estranged I have become to my brothers, \q and a foreigner to the sons of my mother.
en.B: My own brothers treat me as a stranger; \q to my mother's sons I am an outsider.
en.R: Even my brothers act as if they do not know me. \q My own family treats me like a foreigner.

decisions.choice: the sons of my mother: my closest family
decisions.reason: Sons of the same mother were the closest of brothers in a household with more than one wife. Even they have turned away (Job 19:13-15).
John 7:5 says that Jesus' brothers did not believe in him.

source.text: כִּֽי־קִנְאַ֣ת בֵּיתְךָ֣ אֲכָלָ֑תְנִי וְחֶרְפּ֥וֹת ח֝וֹרְפֶ֗יךָ נָפְל֥וּ עָלָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: For zeal for your house has consumed me, and [the] reproaches of those who reproach you have fallen on me.

en.L: For zeal for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} house has consumed me, \q and the reproaches of those who reproach {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have fallen on me.
en.B: Passion for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} house burns me up, \q and the taunts aimed at {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have landed on me.
en.R: I care so much about {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} house that it eats me up inside. \q When people insult {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, the insults fall on me.

decisions.choice: John 2:17: "Zeal for your house will consume me"
decisions.reason: When Jesus drove the traders out of the temple, his disciples remembered this line (John 2:17).

decisions.choice: Romans 15:3: "The insults of those who insult you fell on me"
decisions.reason: Paul quotes the second half of the verse: Christ did not please himself, but bore the insults aimed at God.
The word (qin'ah) is intense, jealous devotion; here his love for God's house (the temple) that will not let it be dishonored.

source.text: וָאֶבְכֶּ֣ה בַצּ֣וֹם נַפְשִׁ֑י וַתְּהִ֖י לַחֲרָפ֣וֹת לִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And I wept with fasting my soul, and it became reproaches to me.

en.L: And I wept, [humbling] my soul with fasting, \q and it became reproaches to me.
en.B: I wept and went without food, \q and for that they mocked me.
en.R: When I cried and went without food, \q people made fun of me.

decisions.choice: I wept with fasting my soul: I wept and fasted
alternatives: I humbled my soul with fasting (the ancient Greek translation)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is short: "I wept, in fasting, my soul". It seems to mean he wept and fasted with his whole self. The ancient Greek translation reads "I bowed my soul with fasting", as in 35:13.

decisions.choice: fasting: going without food in grief and prayer
decisions.reason: People fasted to mourn, to repent, or to plead with God (35:13; 2 Samuel 12:16).
Literal supplies the verb that "fasting my soul" implies (m1).

source.text: וָאֶתְּנָ֣ה לְבוּשִׁ֣י שָׂ֑ק וָאֱהִ֖י לָהֶ֣ם לְמָשָֽׁל׃

records.literal_gloss: And I made my clothing sackcloth, and I became to them a byword.

en.L: And I made sackcloth my clothing, \q and I became a byword to them.
en.B: When I put on sackcloth for clothing, \q they made me the butt of their sayings.
en.R: When I wore rough sackcloth to show my sorrow, \q they joked about me.

decisions.choice: sackcloth: rough cloth worn in mourning
decisions.reason: Sackcloth, made of goat's hair, was worn in grief and repentance (35:13; Genesis 37:34).
The word (mashal) is a proverb; here his name has become a saying people use to mock (44:15).
Readable says why sackcloth was worn.

source.text: יָשִׂ֣יחוּ בִ֭י יֹ֣שְׁבֵי שָׁ֑עַר וּ֝נְגִינ֗וֹת שׁוֹתֵ֥י שֵׁכָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: They talk about me, those who sit [in the] gate, and [I am the] songs of drinkers of strong drink.

en.L: Those who sit [in the] gate talk about me, \q and [I am the] songs of the drinkers of strong drink.
en.B: The people who sit at the city gate gossip about me, \q and drunkards sing songs mocking me.
en.R: The leaders who sit at the city gate talk about me. \q Drunks make up songs about me.

decisions.choice: those who sit in the gate: the town's leaders
decisions.reason: The open space at the city gate was where elders judged cases and people met (Ruth 4:1-2; Proverbs 31:23). He is mocked by the leading men and by drunkards alike.
The word (neginot) is music on strings; here, songs made up to mock him (Lamentations 3:14).

alternatives: those who sit in the gate
decisions.reason: Readable says who sat at the gate (m1).

source.text: וַאֲנִ֤י תְפִלָּתִֽי־לְךָ֨׀יְהוָ֡ה עֵ֤ת רָצ֗וֹן אֱלֹהִ֥ים בְּרָב־חַסְדֶּ֑ךָ עֲ֝נֵ֗נִי בֶּאֱמֶ֥ת יִשְׁעֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: But I, my prayer [is] to you, YHWH, [at a] time of favor; God, in [the] greatness of your loyal love answer me in [the] faithfulness of your salvation.

en.L: But I — my prayer [is] to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, [at a] time of favor; \q God, in the greatness of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love, \q answer me in the faithfulness of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} salvation.
en.B: But as for me, I pray to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, at a time {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will accept; \q God, in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} great loyal love, \q answer me with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithful rescue.
en.R: But I keep praying to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}. Now is the time to show me kindness. \q God, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithful love is so great! \q Answer me, because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are faithful to save.

decisions.choice: a time of favor: a time when God is pleased to answer
alternatives: may this be a time of your favor
decisions.reason: The words describe the right moment, when God accepts a prayer and acts (Isaiah 49:8, quoted in 2 Corinthians 6:2). He prays that this will be such a time.
The word (chesed) is love that keeps faith within a bond: the LORD's committed, dependable kindness to his people. Literal and Balanced say "loyal love".

decisions.choice: the faithfulness of your salvation: your dependable rescue
decisions.reason: God's rescue is sure because he is faithful ('emet) to his promises.
Readable uses plainer words for chesed (see the meaning decision).

source.text: הַצִּילֵ֣נִי מִ֭טִּיט וְאַל־אֶטְבָּ֑עָה אִנָּצְלָ֥ה מִ֝שֹּֽׂנְאַ֗י וּמִמַּֽעֲמַקֵּי־מָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: Deliver me from [the] mud, and let me not sink; let me be delivered from those who hate me and from [the] depths of water.

en.L: Deliver me from [the] mud, and let me not sink; \q let me be delivered from those who hate me and from [the] depths of water.
en.B: Pull me out of the mud, and do not let me go under; \q let me be snatched away from those who hate me, out of the deep water.
en.R: Pull me out of the mud! Do not let me sink. \q Save me from people who hate me. Get me out of this deep water.

decisions.choice: the mud and the deep water: his enemies
decisions.reason: The pictures of verses 2-3 return, now set beside "those who hate me": the danger he is drowning in is the hatred of his enemies.
The verb (natsal) is to pull someone out of danger.

source.text: אַל־תִּשְׁטְפֵ֤נִי׀שִׁבֹּ֣לֶת מַ֭יִם וְאַל־תִּבְלָעֵ֣נִי מְצוּלָ֑ה וְאַל־תֶּאְטַר־עָלַ֖י בְּאֵ֣ר פִּֽיהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Let not [the] flood of water sweep over me, and let not [the] deep swallow me, and let not [the] pit close its mouth over me.

en.L: Let not the flood of water sweep over me, and let not the deep swallow me, \q and let not the pit close its mouth over me.
en.B: Do not let the flood waters wash over me or the deep gulp me down, \q or the pit shut its mouth on me.
en.R: Do not let the flood wash over me. Do not let the deep water swallow me. \q Do not let the grave close its mouth over me.

decisions.choice: the pit: a well, the grave
decisions.reason: The word (be'er) is a well or a pit; it stands for the grave and the place of the dead (55:24). A pit that closes its mouth leaves no way out.
Readable says what the pit stands for (m1).

source.text: עֲנֵ֣נִי יְ֭הוָה כִּי־ט֣וֹב חַסְדֶּ֑ךָ כְּרֹ֥ב רַ֝חֲמֶ֗יךָ פְּנֵ֣ה אֵלָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Answer me, YHWH, for good [is] your loyal love; according to [the] greatness of your compassions turn to me.

en.L: Answer me, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, for good [is] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love; \q according to the greatness of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} compassion turn to me.
en.B: Answer me, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, because {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love is good; \q in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} great compassion, turn toward me.
en.R: Answer me, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, because {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithful love is so good. \q You are full of kindness, so turn and look at me.

decisions.reason: The word (chesed) is love that keeps faith within a bond: the LORD's committed, dependable kindness to his people. Literal and Balanced say "loyal love".
The word (rachamim) is related to the word for womb: the tender love of a mother or father (103:13).

decisions.choice: turn to me: look on me with favor
decisions.reason: As in 25:16, to turn toward someone is to pay attention and help.
Readable uses plainer words for chesed (see the meaning decision).

source.text: וְאַל־תַּסְתֵּ֣ר פָּ֭נֶיךָ מֵֽעַבְדֶּ֑ךָ כִּֽי־צַר־לִ֝֗י מַהֵ֥ר עֲנֵֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: And do not hide your face from your servant, for I am in distress; quickly answer me.

en.L: And do not hide {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} face from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, \q for I am in distress; quickly answer me.
en.B: Do not turn away from me, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant; \q I am hard pressed, so be quick to answer me.
en.R: I am {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant. Do not turn away from me. \q I am in trouble, so answer me quickly!

decisions.choice: hide your face: turn away, refuse to help
decisions.reason: For God to hide his face is to withdraw his presence and favor (13:2; 27:9).

decisions.choice: your servant: one who belongs to God
decisions.reason: The psalmist calls himself God's servant ('eved), one who serves and depends on his master.
Balanced and Readable say what the picture means (m1).

source.text: קָרְבָ֣ה אֶל־נַפְשִׁ֣י גְאָלָ֑הּ לְמַ֖עַן אֹיְבַ֣י פְּדֵֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: Draw near to my soul; redeem it; because of my enemies ransom me.

en.L: Draw near to my soul; redeem it; \q because of my enemies ransom me.
en.B: Come close to me and buy me back; \q set me free because of my enemies.
en.R: Come near and save my life. \q Set me free, so that my enemies will not win.

decisions.choice: redeem, ransom: buy back and set free
decisions.reason: Both verbs come from family and legal life. To redeem (ga'al) is what a close relative did for a kinsman in debt or slavery (Leviticus 25:25, 48); to ransom (padah) is to pay the price that sets someone free.

decisions.choice: because of my enemies: so they do not triumph
decisions.reason: God's rescue will show the enemies that the one they mocked was not abandoned (verse 7).
Balanced and Readable say "me" or "my life" for nefesh.

decisions.choice: so that my enemies will not win
decisions.reason: Readable says how the enemies are the reason (m2).

source.text: אַתָּ֤ה יָדַ֗עְתָּ חֶרְפָּתִ֣י וּ֭בָשְׁתִּי וּכְלִמָּתִ֑י נֶ֝גְדְּךָ֗ כָּל־צוֹרְרָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: You know my reproach and my shame and my humiliation; before you [are] all my foes.

en.L: You know my reproach and my shame and my humiliation; \q before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} [are] all my foes.
en.B: You know the scorn I bear, my shame and my disgrace; \q every one of my enemies is in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} sight.
en.R: You know how they insult me, shame me and make me look foolish. \q You see all my enemies.

decisions.choice: you know: an appeal to what God sees
decisions.reason: Nothing has to be explained: God sees the shame and every enemy (verse 6).
His enemies are all before God's eyes, known to him.

source.text: חֶרְפָּ֤ה׀שָֽׁבְרָ֥ה לִבִּ֗י וָֽאָ֫נ֥וּשָׁה וָאֲקַוֶּ֣ה לָנ֣וּד וָאַ֑יִן וְ֝לַמְנַחֲמִ֗ים וְלֹ֣א מָצָֽאתִי׃

records.literal_gloss: Reproach has broken my heart, and I am sick; and I waited for sympathy, and there was none, and for comforters, and I did not find [any].

en.L: Reproach has broken my heart, and I am sick; \q and I waited for sympathy, but there was none, \q and for comforters, but I did not find [any].
en.B: Scorn has broken my heart, leaving me sick; \q I hoped someone would pity me, but no one did, \q that someone would comfort me, but there was no one to be found.
en.R: Their insults have broken my heart. I feel sick. \q I hoped someone would feel sorry for me, but no one did. \q I looked for someone to comfort me, but I found no one.

decisions.choice: I am sick: weak and ill
decisions.reason: The verb (nush) is found only here; it seems to mean to be sick or weak.

decisions.choice: sympathy: shaking the head in pity
decisions.reason: The verb (nud) is to nod or shake the head, the gesture of someone who shares in another's grief (Job 2:11; 42:11).
Compare Lamentations 1:2, 9: Jerusalem has "no one to comfort her".

source.text: וַיִּתְּנ֣וּ בְּבָרוּתִ֣י רֹ֑אשׁ וְ֝לִצְמָאִ֗י יַשְׁק֥וּנִי חֹֽמֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: And they put in my food poison, and for my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.

en.L: And they put poison in my food, \q and for my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.
en.B: They put bitter poison into my food, \q and for my thirst they handed me sour wine.
en.R: They put poison in my food. \q When I was thirsty, they gave me sour wine.

decisions.reason: The word (rosh) is a bitter, poisonous plant, often paired with wormwood (Deuteronomy 29; Lamentations 3:19).
The word (chomets) is wine gone sour; it was a cheap drink, not a kindness to a thirsty man (Proverbs 10:26).

decisions.choice: the cross: gall and sour wine
decisions.reason: At the crucifixion Jesus was offered wine mixed with gall, and then sour wine on a sponge (Matthew 27:34, 48; Mark 15:36; John 19:28-30). The Gospels tell it in words that recall this verse.
Balanced and Readable say what the drink was (m2).

source.text: יְהִֽי־שֻׁלְחָנָ֣ם לִפְנֵיהֶ֣ם לְפָ֑ח וְלִשְׁלוֹמִ֥ים לְמוֹקֵֽשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: Let their table before them become a trap, and for [those at] peace a snare.

en.L: Let their table before them become a trap, \q and for [those at] peace a snare.
en.B: May the meal set before them become a trap for them, \q a snare when they feel secure.
en.R: Let their own feasts become a trap for them. \q When they feel safe, let them be caught.

decisions.choice: for those at peace: when they feel secure
decisions.reason: The word (shelomim) can mean "those at peace", allies, or the peace offerings eaten at a feast. The ancient Greek translation read it with other vowels as "repayment", and Romans 11:9 follows that reading.
Paul quotes verses 23-24, from the Greek, of those in Israel who did not believe: "Let their table become a snare and a trap, a stumbling block and a retribution for them."

Verses 23-29 ask God to punish the enemies. The psalmist does not take revenge himself but hands the case to God, the judge (Romans 12:19). The table that they spread with poison for him (verse 22) is to become their own trap.

source.text: תֶּחְשַׁ֣כְנָה עֵ֭ינֵיהֶם מֵרְא֑וֹת וּ֝מָתְנֵ֗יהֶם תָּמִ֥יד הַמְעַֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: Let their eyes be darkened from seeing, and their loins continually make shake.

en.L: Let their eyes be darkened from seeing, \q and make their loins shake continually.
en.B: May their eyes grow dim until they cannot see; \q make their bodies tremble without end.
en.R: Make their eyes go dark so they cannot see. \q Make them shake with fear all the time.

decisions.reason: The loins or hips are where strength sits; when they shake, a person collapses in fear and weakness (Nahum 2; Ezekiel 29:7).

decisions.choice: make shake: a request to God
decisions.reason: The verb is a command addressed to God; the first half is a wish.
Paul quotes this verse from the Greek: "Let their eyes be darkened so that they cannot see, and bend their backs forever."
Readable says what the picture means (m1).

source.text: שְׁפָךְ־עֲלֵיהֶ֥ם זַעְמֶ֑ךָ וַחֲר֥וֹן אַ֝פְּךָ֗ יַשִּׂיגֵֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Pour out on them your indignation, and [the] burning of your anger, let it overtake them.

en.L: Pour out on them {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} indignation, \q and let the burning of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anger overtake them.
en.B: Pour {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} fury out on them; \q let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} blazing anger catch up with them.
en.R: Let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anger pour down on them. \q Let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} burning anger catch them.

decisions.reason: The word (za'am) is anger that boils over, here God's just anger at those who persecute the innocent.

decisions.choice: the burning of your anger: blazing anger
decisions.reason: Anger is pictured as fire (2:12; 78:49).

source.text: תְּהִי־טִֽירָתָ֥ם נְשַׁמָּ֑ה בְּ֝אָהֳלֵיהֶ֗ם אַל־יְהִ֥י יֹשֵֽׁב׃

records.literal_gloss: Let their encampment be desolate; in their tents let there be no one dwelling.

en.L: Let their encampment be desolate; \q in their tents let there be no one dwelling.
en.B: Let their camp become a wasteland, \q with nobody living in their tents.
en.R: Let their homes become empty ruins. \q Let no one live in their tents.

decisions.reason: Peter applies this verse, together with 109:8, to Judas: "Let his dwelling be deserted, and let no one live in it."

decisions.choice: encampment: a camp or walled settlement
decisions.reason: The word (tirah) is a camp or walled village, the home of a family or clan.

decisions.choice: empty tents: a family wiped out
decisions.reason: A home with no one living in it means that the family line has come to an end.

source.text: כִּֽי־אַתָּ֣ה אֲשֶׁר־הִכִּ֣יתָ רָדָ֑פוּ וְאֶל־מַכְא֖וֹב חֲלָלֶ֣יךָ יְסַפֵּֽרוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: For you, [the one] whom you struck they have pursued, and about [the] pain of your wounded [ones] they talk.

en.L: For [the one] whom {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} struck, they have pursued, \q and about the pain of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} wounded ones they talk.
en.B: For they chase down the one {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have struck, \q and gossip about the pain of the people {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have wounded.
en.R: They chase the one {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have struck down. \q They make fun of the pain of those {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have wounded.

decisions.choice: the one you struck: suffering God allowed
decisions.reason: The psalmist sees his suffering as coming from God's hand (verse 8 says it is for God's sake). Instead of pity the enemies hunt down the one already struck (Isaiah 53:4).

alternatives: they add to the pain (the ancient Greek translation)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says they "tell" or talk of the pain of the wounded, gloating over it. The ancient Greek translation read a similar verb, "they added to" the pain.
The pronoun is written out for emphasis: it was God himself who struck.

source.text: תְּֽנָה־עָ֭וֺן עַל־עֲוֺנָ֑ם וְאַל־יָ֝בֹ֗אוּ בְּצִדְקָתֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Put guilt on their guilt, and let them not come into your righteousness.

en.L: Put guilt upon their guilt, \q and let them not come into {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} righteousness.
en.B: Add guilt to their guilt; \q let them have no share in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} saving justice.
en.R: Count every one of their sins against them. \q Do not let them go free when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} judge.

decisions.choice: put guilt on their guilt: hold every sin against them
decisions.reason: The word ('awon) means both guilt and its punishment. Let none of their wrongs be overlooked.

decisions.choice: come into your righteousness: be acquitted by you
decisions.reason: God's righteousness (tsedaqah) here is his verdict that someone is in the right, which leads to rescue. The prayer is that they not be declared innocent.

decisions.choice: do not let them go free when you judge
alternatives: let them not come into your righteousness
decisions.reason: Readable says what the phrase means (m2).

source.text: יִ֭מָּחֽוּ מִסֵּ֣פֶר חַיִּ֑ים וְעִ֥ם צַ֝דִּיקִ֗ים אַל־יִכָּתֵֽבוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Let them be wiped out of [the] book of life, and with [the] righteous let them not be written.

en.L: Let them be wiped out of [the] book of life, \q and with [the] righteous let them not be written.
en.B: May their names be erased from the book of life, \q never to be entered with the righteous.
en.R: Let their names be erased from the book of life. \q Do not let them be listed with people who do what is right.

decisions.choice: the book of life: God's list of the living
decisions.reason: Like a city's list of citizens, God's book holds the names of those who live before him (Exodus 32:32-33; Isaiah 4:3). To be wiped out of it is to die. The New Testament speaks of the book of life for eternal life (Philippians 4:3; Revelation 3:5).

decisions.choice: the righteous: those in the right with God
decisions.reason: The tsaddiqim are those who do what is right and belong to God's people.
Balanced and Readable say what is written in the book.

source.text: וַ֭אֲנִי עָנִ֣י וְכוֹאֵ֑ב יְשׁוּעָתְךָ֖ אֱלֹהִ֣ים תְּשַׂגְּבֵֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: And I [am] afflicted and in pain; your salvation, God, let it set me on high.

en.L: But I [am] afflicted and in pain; \q let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} salvation, God, set me on high.
en.B: But I am poor and hurting; \q let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} saving help, God, lift me up to safety.
en.R: But I am poor and in pain. \q God, save me and keep me safe.

decisions.choice: set me on high: put me out of reach
decisions.reason: To be set on high is to be placed safely above danger, like a fortress on a height (20:2; 59:2; 91:14).

decisions.choice: but I: the turn to hope
decisions.reason: The "I" stands first in contrast with the enemies: they are to be wiped out, he asks to be lifted up.
The word ('ani) means poor and afflicted, someone with no power of his own.

source.text: אֲהַֽלְלָ֣ה שֵׁם־אֱלֹהִ֣ים בְּשִׁ֑יר וַאֲגַדְּלֶ֥נּוּ בְתוֹדָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: I will praise [the] name of God with a song, and I will magnify him with thanksgiving.

en.L: I will praise the name of God with a song, \q and I will magnify {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with thanksgiving.
en.B: With a song I will praise God's name \q and proclaim {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} greatness with thanksgiving.
en.R: I will sing to praise God. \q I will thank {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and tell how great {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is.

decisions.choice: I will praise: the vow of thanks
decisions.reason: The psalm turns from lament to praise, sure that God will answer.

decisions.choice: thanksgiving: a song or offering of thanks
decisions.reason: The word (todah) is both a thanksgiving song and a thank offering (50:14, 23).
To magnify God (gadal, intensive) is to tell how great he is (34:4).

source.text: וְתִיטַ֣ב לַֽ֭יהוָה מִשּׁ֥וֹר פָּ֗ר מַקְרִ֥ן מַפְרִֽיס׃

records.literal_gloss: And it will be good to YHWH more than an ox, a bull having horns, having hooves.

en.L: And it will please {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} more than an ox, \q a bull with horns [and] hooves.
en.B: That will delight {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} more than an ox \q or a young bull with full-grown horns and hooves.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will like this more than the sacrifice of an ox, \q even a full-grown bull with horns and hooves.

decisions.reason: Thankful praise pleases God more than the costliest animal offering (50:13-14; 51:18-19). The psalm does not reject sacrifice but puts the heart first.

decisions.choice: with horns and hooves: a full-grown, clean animal
decisions.reason: A bull with grown horns is mature and valuable; split hooves mark it as a clean animal fit for sacrifice (Leviticus 11:3).
Readable makes clear that the ox is an offering.

source.text: רָא֣וּ עֲנָוִ֣ים יִשְׂמָ֑חוּ דֹּרְשֵׁ֥י אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים וִיחִ֥י לְבַבְכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: The humble have seen; they rejoice; seekers of God, let your heart live.

en.L: The humble have seen; they rejoice; \q you who seek God, let your heart live.
en.B: The humble will see it and be glad; \q you who seek God, take heart and live!
en.R: Humble people will see what God has done and be glad. \q You who look to God, be encouraged!

decisions.choice: the humble: the lowly who depend on God
decisions.reason: The 'anawim are the poor and humble who look to God for help (22:27; 37:11).

decisions.choice: let your heart live: take new courage
decisions.reason: A heart that "lives" is revived and encouraged (22:27).
The verb is past in form, but it speaks of what the humble will surely see when God rescues the psalmist.
Readable says what they see.

source.text: כִּֽי־שֹׁמֵ֣עַ אֶל־אֶבְיוֹנִ֣ים יְהוָ֑ה וְאֶת־אֲ֝סִירָ֗יו לֹ֣א בָזָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: For YHWH listens to [the] needy, and his prisoners he does not despise.

en.L: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} listens to the needy, \q and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} prisoners {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does not despise.
en.B: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} hears the poor \q and does not look down on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people in chains.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} listens to people in need. \q He does not turn {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} back on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people who are in prison.

decisions.choice: his prisoners: his people in captivity
decisions.reason: The prisoners are God's own people in chains, perhaps those taken into exile, or those in prison because of their loyalty to him (102:21; 107:10).

decisions.choice: the needy: the poor who have no helper
decisions.reason: The 'evyonim are the needy, a word often paired with the afflicted (verse 30).

source.text: יְֽ֭הַלְלוּהוּ שָׁמַ֣יִם וָאָ֑רֶץ יַ֝מִּ֗ים וְֽכָל־רֹמֵ֥שׂ בָּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Let them praise him, heaven and earth, [the] seas and everything that moves in them.

en.L: Let heaven and earth praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \q the seas and everything that moves in them.
en.B: Let the heavens and the earth praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \q the seas and all that swarms in them.
en.R: Let the sky and the earth praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \q Let the seas and every creature in them praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} too.

decisions.reason: Heaven, earth and sea name the whole of creation (Exodus 20:11; 96:11; 148).
The verb (ramas) is used of creatures that move about in great numbers (Genesis 1:21; 104:25).

source.text: כִּ֤י אֱלֹהִ֨ים׀י֘וֹשִׁ֤יעַ צִיּ֗וֹן וְ֭יִבְנֶה עָרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֑ה וְיָ֥שְׁבוּ שָׁ֝֗ם וִירֵשֽׁוּהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: For God will save Zion and build [the] cities of Judah, and they will dwell there and possess it,

en.L: For God will save Zion and build the cities of Judah, \q and they will dwell there and possess it,
en.B: For God will rescue Zion and build up Judah's towns again; \q {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people will live there and hold it as their own,
en.R: God will rescue Jerusalem and rebuild the towns of Judah. \q His people will live there, and the land will be theirs.

decisions.choice: Zion and the towns of Judah rebuilt
decisions.reason: The ending looks to a time when Judah's towns lie in ruins and must be rebuilt, as after the fall of Jerusalem (Isaiah 44:26). One sufferer's rescue becomes a sign of hope for the whole people.
The promise continues in verse 37, so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.
Balanced and Readable say who "they" are: God's servants (verse 37).
Readable gives the familiar name of the city; Zion is the hill on which the temple stood.

source.text: וְזֶ֣רַע עֲ֭בָדָיו יִנְחָל֑וּהָ וְאֹהֲבֵ֥י שְׁ֝מ֗וֹ יִשְׁכְּנוּ־בָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: and [the] offspring of his servants will inherit it, and those who love his name will dwell in it.

en.L: and the offspring of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servants will inherit it, \q and those who love {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name will dwell in it.
en.B: the descendants of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servants will receive it as their inheritance, \q and all who love {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name will make their home in it.
en.R: The children of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servants will receive it as their own. \q Everyone who loves {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name will live there.

decisions.choice: inherit: receive as a family possession
decisions.reason: The land is passed down as an inheritance from God (37:29).

decisions.choice: those who love his name: those who love God
decisions.reason: God's name stands for God himself (5:12).
